dev.title: Developers — Yoto Icons Catalogue
dev.description: Public API documentation: data endpoints, schemas and code examples. All endpoints are public, free and without API key.
dev.stability: The API is static (GitHub Pages). No strict rate limit, but be reasonable (< 100 req/min recommended).
dev.quickstartContent: Use the base URL /icons-catalogue/ to access API endpoints. The full manifest is available at /icons-catalogue/dist/summary.json.
dev.endpointSummaryDesc: Catalog manifest with total icon count and category counters.
dev.endpointSummaryFilesDesc: Metadata summary with source counters (yotopixels, yotoicons, yoto-official).
dev.endpointSearchIndexDesc: Lunr search index (~500 KB) for instant client-side search.
dev.endpointCombinedDesc: Full icons index (~21 MB) with all detailed metadata.
dev.schemaIconDesc: The API returns JSON objects. The base icon schema includes fields: id, source, tags, artist, title, preview_image, download_url, category, subcategory, downloads, date_added, license, and optional metadata.
dev.schemaSummaryDesc: The summary schema includes: schemaVersion, total, byCategory, and bySource.
dev.codeExamplesContent: Usage examples are available in the Resources section with links to Node.js source code and TypeScript types.
dev.performanceContent: The lunr search index (~500 KB) is included in /dist/search-index.json for instant client-side search. All endpoints include Cache-Control and stale-while-revalidate headers. Cache client-side. The API is static (GitHub Pages) with no strict rate limit, but a limit of 100 requests/minute is recommended.
dev.versioningContent: The API uses schemaVersion versioning (format YYYY.MM.DD-N). Schema changes are indicated in the summary JSON.
dev.stabilityContent: The API is stable: /api/catalog* and /search.json endpoints are stable. The /api/health.json and /search-index.json endpoints may evolve to add metrics.
dev.licenceContent: The metadata and code of this catalogue are licensed under MIT — free for commercial reuse.
dev.attributionContent: Mention the catalogue in your app credits or on the about page.
dev.contentsContent: Download URLs and preview images belong to their respective creators. The API only provides metadata.
